boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented Samford spaces for studying, meals, recreation, and campus gatherings.

cards.entity_name: Harwell G. Davis University Library Third-Floor Study Rooms
cards.title: Third-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis University Library
cards.notes: For a quiet solo or two-person session, ask at the first-floor circulation desk for a key and use the room in two-hour blocks.
cards.short_summary: Individual rooms for one or two Samford students.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says its third-floor study rooms serve one or two Samford students and are available first come, first served.
cards.source_title: Frequently Answered Questions — Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: Samford students; keys are handled through the circulation desk. Check library access and current hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Harwell G. Davis University Library Second-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Second-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Harwell G. Davis University Library
cards.notes: Bring at least one study partner, then check out a room key from circulation for a focused two-hour group-work block.
cards.short_summary: Locked group rooms designed for two or more students.
cards.evidence_claim: The library policy identifies second-floor study rooms as group spaces for two or more students, with keys checked out at circulation.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms Policy — Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: Available to Samford undergraduate and graduate students; first come, first served, with a two-hour checkout block.

cards.entity_name: Harwell G. Davis University Library Media Rooms 111–115
cards.title: Media Rooms 111–115
cards.subtitle: First floor, Harwell G. Davis University Library
cards.notes: Use these rooms for reserve audiovisual material; group study is possible when other study rooms are full and equipment is not needed.
cards.short_summary: First-floor audiovisual rooms that can accommodate group study.
cards.evidence_claim: The library designates Media Rooms 111–115 for audiovisual use and permits first-come group study when other study rooms are occupied.
cards.source_title: Media Rooms Policy — Samford University Library
cards.access_notes: Academic-media use takes priority; study users may be asked to relocate if equipment is needed.

cards.entity_name: Harwell G. Davis University Library Computer Classroom/Lab
cards.title: Library Computer Classroom/Lab
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Harwell G. Davis University Library
cards.notes: Head to the lower level when you need the library’s mapped computer classroom/lab; confirm building hours before setting up.
cards.short_summary: A mapped lower-level computer space in Davis Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s lower-level floor map lists a Computer Classroom/Lab in the Harwell G. Davis library building.
cards.access_notes: Located on the lower level; library access and hours govern use.

cards.title: Student Commons
cards.subtitle: Ralph W. Beeson University Center
cards.notes: Use the University Center’s student-commons area as a central stop between classes, then check the building’s current access arrangements.
cards.short_summary: A named common area inside Samford’s student-life hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford’s event-planning spaces page lists Student Commons in Beeson University Center, and the university describes the center as a hub of student life.
cards.access_notes: Inside the University Center; observe building access and any event reservations.

cards.title: University Center Food Court
cards.subtitle: First floor, Ralph W. Beeson University Center
cards.notes: Meet a classmate for a meal or coffee at the first-floor food court, which Samford lists with several dining counters.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor collection of campus dining counters.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford identifies the Beeson University Center food court as a first-floor location with Boar’s Head, Chick-fil-A, Hissho Sushi, Moe’s, O’Henry’s, Samford Grill, and Simply to Go.
cards.access_notes: Food service is in the University Center; availability may vary with the academic calendar.

cards.title: The Caf
cards.subtitle: Ralph W. Beeson University Center
cards.notes: Plan a campus meal at The Caf, then review dining access or meal-plan details through Samford before relying on it.
cards.short_summary: The University Center’s mapped dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford’s campus map lists The Caf as the Dining Hall within Ralph W. Beeson University Center.
cards.access_notes: Located in Beeson University Center; dining access and service vary by university schedule.

cards.title: Seibert Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation, Wellness and Athletics Complex
cards.notes: Choose a court, track, studio, billiards table, or fitness area for a recreation break; verify the current facility schedule first.
cards.short_summary: A four-story recreation complex with courts, studios, and shared activity areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford says Seibert Hall contains courts, fitness areas, an elevated jogging track, studios, billiards, a coffeehouse, and a 24-hour market.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to Campus Recreation membership, guest rules, event reservations, and changing hours.

cards.title: Intramural Fields
cards.subtitle: Intramural/Recreation Complex
cards.notes: Join an outdoor intramural game or use the courts and covered pavilion when the area is available through Campus Recreation.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor fields with student recreation facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford identifies the intramural fields as the home for outdoor intramurals and lists soccer, flag football, softball, Ultimate Frisbee, sand volleyball, basketball, and a covered pavilion.
cards.access_notes: Coordinate with Campus Recreation and observe field availability for intramural or informal use.

cards.title: Reid Chapel
cards.subtitle: Samford University campus
cards.notes: Check the university calendar for a convocation or concert, then arrive through the appropriate public entrance for that event.
cards.short_summary: A campus chapel used for convocations and concerts.
cards.evidence_claim: Samford describes A. Hamilton Reid Chapel as the site of many convocations and concerts.
cards.access_notes: Event attendance and building access depend on the scheduled program.
